title: 🎧 Listening Section 1 — Everyday Conversations

sections.heading: What to expect
sections.body:
Section 1 is a conversation between two people in an everyday social context:
• Booking a service (hotel, repair shop)
• Registering for a course
• Arranging accommodation
• Making an enquiry

The questions follow the order of the conversation. You'll answer multiple choice, form completion, or short answer questions.

sections.heading: Key listening skills
sections.body:
• Listen for NUMBERS carefully — prices, dates, times, phone numbers
• Spell-check names — the answer may be spelled out
• Predict answer types BEFORE listening: "Q1 asks for a price → listen for £ or a number"
• Watch for CORRECTIONS: "No, it's Thursday, not Tuesday" — the CORRECTION is the answer

highlight: Section 1 is the easiest section. Most students can score 9/10 here with good technique. Don't rush — the gaps between questions give you reading time.

title: 🔢 Number & Date Traps
body:
Numbers are the most commonly missed answers in Section 1.

Traps to watch:
• "It's £45... no wait, £54" → 54 is the answer
• "Monday the 15th" → might need just "15th" or "Monday"
• Phone numbers: write every digit as you hear it
• Addresses: "14 Bridge Street" → don't write "14th"

Always check: does your answer fit the space grammatically?

quick.label: Write while listening — don't rely on memory

question: In Listening Section 1, when should you read the questions?
options: During the 10 minutes before the section begins
Before the recording starts, during the reading time
correct: Before the recording starts, during the reading time
explanation:
You get 30 seconds of reading time before each section. Use every second to:
• Read ALL questions carefully
• Underline keywords
• Predict the type of answer (name, number, day, etc.)

This preparation is what separates Band 7 from Band 9 in listening.

question: You hear: "The fee is £120... actually, let me check — it's £102." What should you write?
explanation:
Always write the FINAL/CORRECTED figure.

Speakers often self-correct in natural conversation: "No, wait...", "Actually...", "I mean..."

The correction is ALWAYS the intended answer. This is a deliberate trap in IELTS listening tests.

sentence: In the listening test, you have _______ minutes at the end to transfer your answers to the answer sheet.
explanation:
You get 10 minutes at the end of the entire Listening test to copy your answers to the answer sheet. Use this time to:
• Transfer carefully (don't rush)
• Check spelling
• Check grammar (singular/plural, correct tense)
• Fill in any blanks you missed

question: Which strategy is MOST effective for Section 1 multiple choice?
options: Listen for the exact words in the options
Listen for the meaning and eliminate wrong options
Only focus on Option A and B
correct: Listen for the meaning and eliminate wrong options
explanation:
The recording almost never uses the exact words from the options — it paraphrases.

Best approach:
1. Read all options before listening
2. Cross out options that are clearly contradicted
3. Mark the one that matches the meaning

Option A and B are deliberately designed to seem correct at first.
